source.paper: Kang, Kim & Kim, Quantum Computing Based Design of Multivariate Porous Materials, ACS Cent. Sci. (2025)
source.inputs: Table S2 (characteristic linker lengths), Table S3 and Fig. S2 (site graphs, edge distances)
source.reference: Fig. 5 / Fig. S3: the lowest-Hamiltonian configuration of each structure corresponds to the experimental structure

public.description: Three-dimensional multivariate MOF built on Zn4O clusters with a fixed tritopic scaffold; the variable sites hold two ditopic linkers, BDC (short) and BPDC (long), in a 1:1 ratio, on the ith-d net. 6 variable linker sites in the cell; topological edges join sites bridging the same cluster, second_neighbor edges join next-nearest sites.

reference.rule: BDC and BPDC alternate around the site cycle: every edge joins different linkers

kang_hamiltonian.source: Eq. 2, 5-8 and Note S1 (fixed-composition states: ratio and occupancy terms vanish); weights w_ij from Table S3
kang_hamiltonian.formula: sum over edges of w_kind * (L_e - Lbar)^2, L_e = 2 (l_i + l_j), Lbar = mean of L_e over all edges
kang_hamiltonian.published_levels_source: Fig. S3 (distinct Hamiltonian values of fixed-composition states, lowest first)
